# Audio Blackbox

> Audio Blackbox is an open-source (GPL-3.0) Android app that keeps the last minutes of sound in a rolling RAM buffer and writes them to local storage when the user taps Save or starts Live. The buffer is at least 5 minutes, set in 5-minute steps, up to the app's safe memory limit for the selected quality. Recorded audio never leaves the device: the app has no account, no cloud, no ads and sends no usage analytics itself. It runs on Android 10 (API 29) and newer and is free on Google Play, with an optional one-time Pro unlock for unlimited live recording.

Key facts:

- Package name: cc.machado.audioblackbox
- Price: free to install and use. One optional in-app purchase, a one-time Pro unlock (`pro_unlock`), removes the 2-hour limit on live recording time (excluding the buffered past). Everything else, including the retroactive buffer and all quality presets, is free. Early-bird Pro, free: install Audio Blackbox by December 19, 2026 (before December 20, 00:00 Brasília time, UTC−3) and Pro stays unlocked on that device at no cost, for good. The benefit belongs to that installation: uninstalling and reinstalling, or switching devices, does not keep it. The app has no account and no ads, and sends no usage analytics itself.
- This website uses Google Analytics 4 and Microsoft Clarity to measure visits. That applies to the website only, not to the app.
- License: GNU General Public License v3.0, source on GitHub.
- Platform: Android 10 (API 29) and newer.
- Save writes the buffered audio since the last save (the whole buffer the first time) to an AAC (.m4a, default) or Opus (.ogg) file in Recordings/Blackbox (Music/Blackbox on Android 10 and 11).
- Recording runs as a foreground service with a visible notification the whole time.
- Recording other people may require their consent, and the rules differ between countries and states. Users are responsible for checking their local recording laws.

## Use cases

- Musicians & Songwriters: Keep the riff or melody you just improvised, without having pressed record first.
- Journalists & Interviews: A backup for the quote that came before you hit record on your main recorder.
- Students & Lectures: Keep the explanation you just missed, in classes where recording is allowed.
- Memory Aid: Replay instructions, directions or details you were just told. Helpful for anyone who loses track of spoken information, for example people with ADHD. Not a medical device.
- Pocket Audio Dashcam: If something unexpected happens in traffic or on the street, save the minutes leading up to it.
- Ideas & Family Moments: The thought you said out loud, what was just agreed in a meeting you were part of, the first word at the dinner table.

## Save audio format

Save audio format is free, with no Pro unlock required: AAC (default) saves .m4a files with Save, or choose Opus (.ogg) for both Save and Live. AAC (.m4a): wider compatibility. Opus (.ogg): smaller voice files. Some players and messaging apps may not open them. With AAC selected: Live stays AAC (.aac), playable while recording. Wait until recording ends to play Opus audio. If the app closes unexpectedly, saved audio may be recoverable, but the ending may be lost and some players may not open the file. On reopening after an unexpected close, Opus audio already written is recovered; the incomplete final Ogg page is discarded, so the ending may be lost. Opus may be unavailable on some devices; the option is disabled with the reason shown.

## Recording and billing

Live saves the buffered audio from before the tap and continues in a single file: .aac (ADTS) with AAC (default), playable while recording, or .ogg with Opus, which you must wait until recording ends to play. Live recording time is limited to 2 hours on the free plan, then the file is saved automatically. The file can exceed 2 hours because it includes the buffered past. A one-time Pro unlock removes the live time limit.

The app itself sends no audio or usage analytics. Google Play Billing (Play services) communicates with Google to process the optional purchase and check entitlement; its library also sends its own usage and error diagnostics. No ads, account or cloud audio storage.

## Feature docs

- [Capture and memory core](https://alexandre.machado.cc/audio-blackbox/features/01-capture-and-memory-core.html): RAM ring buffer, raw PCM capture and configuration
- [Android integration and background survival](https://alexandre.machado.cc/audio-blackbox/features/02-android-integration.html): microphone foreground service, persistent notification, audio interruptions, permissions and battery optimization
- [Export engine](https://alexandre.machado.cc/audio-blackbox/features/03-export-engine.html): how buffered audio is read and written from RAM to a file, including silence gaps
- [User interface](https://alexandre.machado.cc/audio-blackbox/features/04-user-interface.html): dashboard, main action button, gallery, embedded player and sharing
